defect.symptom: Every semantic action was denied before dispatch as desktop_user_intervened (effect none, verification not_dispatched); three runs reproduced it, including one where the owner kept mouse and keyboard still.
defect.root_cause: InputWatch starts with baseline 0 and act() never called arm(), so every event observed since the tap was installed counted as owner intervention. Fixture activation and window-server focus churn between tap creation and the first check were enough to block dispatch.
defect.fix: arm() immediately after installation (before the focus snapshot and identity re-verification) and split a disabled monitor into desktop_monitor_unavailable so unavailable guards no longer masquerade as owner input.
defect.verification: Same acceptance command on the rebuilt helper passed with set_text ok/value_matches and invoke unknown plus one independently observed click; no receipt was rewritten and nothing was replayed.

official_acceptance.step: independent state wait after the final click

diagnostic.conclusion: Targeted keyboard events reached the fixture (text and selection changed) and the receipts never claimed success for unprovable outcomes. The targeted mouse click was acknowledged but did not press the owned button; the raw acceptance timeout is preserved as an open item for the foreground batch.
